channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Body of 19-Year-Old Woman Exhumed for Re-examination in Kazakhstan
item.description: The body of 19-year-old Madina Rashidkyzy, who died in the Zhambyl region, has been exhumed near Almaty for a re-examination. Relatives doubt her suicide and demand a new forensic examination. The lawyer confirmed the exhumation was requested by the victim's side due to distrust in the initial findings. Pre-trial investigation is underway for incitement to suicide.

item.title: Afghanistan's UN Envoy Calls for Concrete Action to Ensure Justice
item.description: Afghanistan's Permanent Representative to the UN, Naseer Ahmad Faiq, urged concrete action for justice and accountability in Afghanistan. He emphasized enforcing arrest warrants against Taliban officials and protecting victims. Faiq stated that international engagement with the Taliban should not overlook repression and that lasting peace requires justice and credible accountability through action.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Predicts Decline in Credit and Deposit Rates
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank expects credit and deposit rates to decrease over the next 3-4 years. Deputy Chairman Nodirbek Achilov explained that while the main rate is stable, commercial bank lending rates remain high but show a downward trend. Mortgage rates have also fallen, though microloans and unsecured short-term loans still have the highest rates.

item.title: Kazakh Weightlifter Nurgissa Adiletuly Secures Silver at World Championships
item.description: Kazakhstan's Nurgissa Adiletuly won a silver medal in the 95kg category at the World Weightlifting Championships in Ningbo, China. He lifted a total of 399kg, finishing second to Bulgaria's Carlos Nasar, who set a new world record. Adiletuly's performance marks a significant achievement in his career.

item.title: Teacher Killed by Thieves in Logar Province, Afghanistan
item.description: Local sources reported that a teacher named Mohammad Aref was killed by thieves at his home in the Mohammad Agha District of Logar Province on Monday night. The thieves also stole gold and cash from the teacher's residence. This incident follows a recent report of a tribal elder's mysterious death in Samangan Province.

item.title: Astana Police Detain Over 20 Protesters Seeking Meeting with City Authorities
item.description: Over 20 representatives from supplementary education organizations protested at Astana's city hall on November 4, seeking a meeting with officials. Police detained all protesters and took them to a station. The group expressed dissatisfaction with a pilot project implementing Face ID in educational institutions, citing concerns over tender processes and data security with a Russian company.

item.title: Moody's Ratings Assigns Ba1 Rating to BCC Life Insurance Company
item.description: International rating agency Moody's Ratings has assigned a Ba1 rating to BCC Life. This rating reflects the company's financial standing and its outlook within the insurance sector.

item.title: Child Offenses Decline in Kazakhstan; Positive Trends Observed in Several Regions
item.description: The number of offenses against children in Kazakhstan decreased by 3.7% in the first nine months of 2026. Positive trends are noted in the Zhambyl, Atyrau, East Kazakhstan, and Aktobe regions. The Ministry of Education is monitoring regions with past incidents or organizational shortcomings in preventive work.

item.title: Part Two: The Final Moments Before the Fall of Kabul to the Taliban
item.description: The author expresses deep worry about the Taliban's advance on Kabul and the fate of women and girls. As President Ghani reportedly fled the country, fear and anxiety gripped the population. The narrative captures the chaotic final moments before the Taliban's takeover, highlighting the lowering of the national flag and personal accounts of escape.

item.title: Tashkent Police Discover and Dismantle Synthetic Drug Laboratory
item.description: Tashkent police have uncovered a synthetic drug laboratory operating in a rented apartment in the Chilonzor district. The facility was allegedly preparing and distributing synthetic drugs using a 'zakladka' method. Authorities seized 3.5 kg of hashish oil, 600g of hashish, 200g of marijuana, and 8 drug-infused cookies. A criminal case has been initiated against the 22-year-old suspect.

item.title: Kazakhstan May Face Oil Shortage for Refineries Within Three Years, Expert Warns
item.description: An oil and gas market expert warns that Kazakhstan could face a shortage of crude oil for its refineries within three years, even with an annual production of 100 million tons. Declining profitability from mature fields and reduced supplies from independent producers are cited as potential causes. Rising fuel prices are attributed to tax increases aimed at boosting the budget.

item.title: Six sentenced up to 23 years for kidnapping and murder of man in Shymkent
item.description: Six individuals have been sentenced to prison terms ranging from 20 to 23 years for the kidnapping and murder of 40-year-old Vasily Kolesnikov in Shymkent. The court found the defendants guilty of murder, kidnapping, causing grievous bodily harm, and hooliganism. Compensation was awarded to the victim's family.

item.title: Parents of Soldiers Who Died in Service Demand Fair Investigation
item.description: Parents of eight soldiers who died in service held a press conference in Almaty demanding a fair investigation into their children's deaths. They claim evidence points to murder, not suicide, and are calling for systemic reform of the armed forces to prevent future tragedies. The parents are frustrated by the lack of progress and are determined to seek justice.

item.title: Criminal Case Opened Against Kyrgyz Citizens for Remarks on Kenesary Khan
item.description: A criminal case has been initiated against two Kyrgyz students studying in Astana under an academic mobility program. A lawyer filed a complaint after videos circulated showing the students disrespecting national symbols and ancestors. The Ministry of Internal Affairs confirmed an investigation is underway to determine if their actions violated Kazakh law.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Evaluate Teachers Based on Student Safety and Threat Detection
item.description: Kazakhstan is introducing a new criterion for evaluating teachers: their direct involvement in identifying threats and violence against minors. Teachers who promptly detect and report signs of bullying or other dangers will receive positive marks during their professional assessment. This initiative comes amid a general decrease in crimes against children in the country.

item.title: Astana: Children's Club Representatives Detained After Face ID Protest
item.description: About 30 representatives from children's clubs protested mandatory Face ID for attendance at extracurricular activities in Astana. They were detained by police for allegedly disrupting public order after a meeting with education officials.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes "PANA" Project to Offer Refuge to Domestic Violence Victims
item.description: A social project named "PANA" has been proposed in Kazakhstan to prevent domestic violence and persecution. The initiative, raised by Member of Parliament Larisa Li, aims to create a network of safe, accessible locations like small shops and pharmacies where victims can seek immediate refuge. The project focuses on providing a rapid response mechanism.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Establish State Strategic Uranium Reserve by End of 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan, the world's largest uranium producer, plans to create a state strategic uranium reserve by the end of 2027. This reserve aims to secure fuel supplies for future nuclear power plants. The country's strategy includes reserving at least 150,000 metric tons of uranium by 2050.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Establish Veterinary Chamber, Increase Doctor Benefits
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to establish a veterinary chamber to protect the rights and professional interests of veterinarians. The proposed legislation includes annual leave and a wellness allowance equivalent to two salaries. Additional payments will be provided for specialists with scientific degrees, and special clothing will be supplied. The initiative aims to address a shortage of veterinary professionals, particularly in rural areas.

item.title: Kazakh Citizen Arrested for Calling Country a 'Russian Land' in Almaty
item.description: A 40-year-old Kazakh citizen was detained in Almaty for arguing with a security guard and other shoppers, during which he allegedly referred to Kazakhstan as a 'Russian land'. He was subsequently arrested and sentenced to 20 days of administrative detention. The incident occurred in a shopping center.

item.title: Kazakhstan Aims to Reduce Medicine Imports with New Pharmaceutical Plants
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to produce nearly 500 types of medicine domestically by 2034 through eight investment projects totaling $862 million. The initiative aims to create over 1,200 jobs and decrease reliance on imported pharmaceuticals, covering treatments for various diseases. The Ministry of Health reported that domestic production currently accounts for 15% of the market value.

item.title: Chinese Firm Proposes $95 Million Waste-to-Energy Plant in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A subsidiary of China Energy Conservation and Environmental Protection Group (CECEP) is considering a $95 million waste-to-energy plant in southern Kyrgyzstan. The proposed facility would initially process 800 metric tons of waste daily, with potential for expansion. This follows Bishkek's opening of Central Asia's first waste-to-energy plant, also built by a Chinese company.

item.title: Uzbekistan Approves New Methodology for Assessing University Graduate Quality
item.description: Uzbekistan has introduced a new approach to evaluating higher education effectiveness, focusing on graduate employability and professional prospects. The National Agency for Education Quality Assurance has approved a methodology to calculate a graduate quality index, assessing how well universities prepare specialists for the labor market. The index considers employment speed, job stability, income, and job category.

item.title: Kazakhstan Energy Minister Comments on Almaty Thermal Power Plant Construction Delays
item.description: Kazakhstan's Minister of Energy, Yerlan Akkenzhenov, has commented on delays in the construction of thermal power plants (TPPs) 2 and 3 in Almaty. TPP-2 is expected to launch on December 25, 2026, while TPP-3 is significantly behind schedule, with completion anticipated by the end of 2027. The former head of Samruk-Energy was dismissed due to these delays.

item.title: Uzbekistan Inflation: Consumer Estimates Significantly Exceed Official Figures
item.description: A survey by Uzbekistan's Central Bank reveals that consumers estimate inflation at 9.2% for September, considerably higher than the official rate of 6.4%. The survey of 2,726 residents showed a nationwide estimate decrease from August's 10.1%. Tashkent recorded the highest regional estimate at 11.9%, while pensioners estimated 12.5%.

item.title: Tamchi Special Economic Zone Development Focuses on English Law and Special Taxes
item.description: Construction of facilities at the Tamchi Special Financial and Investment Territory (SFIT) in the Issyk-Kul region is ongoing. The project aims to attract international capital and develop financial services, IT, logistics, and tourism, featuring a special legal and tax regime based on English law.

item.title: Modernization Deadline for Almaty Heat Plant 3 Extended
item.description: The completion deadline for the modernization of Heat Plant 3 in Almaty has been postponed. The original timeline for the project has been extended, with further details on the new schedule not yet provided.

item.title: Kazakhstan Energy Minister Addresses Complaints About Unified Time Zone
item.description: Kazakhstan's Energy Minister, Yerlan Akkenzhenov, commented on public complaints regarding insufficient daylight after the country adopted a unified time zone. He stated that overall electricity consumption is growing and he has not personally observed issues with lighting after lunch in Astana.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Raises Inflation Forecast Amid Rising Heating Tariffs
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank has increased its inflation forecast for the end of 2026 from 6.5% to 7%. This adjustment is partly due to anticipated increases in heating and hot water tariffs. The bank stated that all announced changes in regulated prices, including heating tariffs, have been factored into its calculations.

item.title: Polish Power Plants Utilize Kazakh Sunflower Husks for Heating
item.description: Kazakh companies may increase sunflower husk exports to Polish thermal power plants to 250,000 tons annually, nearly 7.5 times the 2025 volume. The National Association of Oilseed Processors attributes this growth to expanded sunflower cultivation, increased domestic processing, and demand for biofuels in Europe. Exports of husks are seen as a complementary development alongside sunflower oil and meal.

item.title: Tajik delegation led by Rustami Emomali visits Uzbekistan, explores New Tashkent project
item.description: A Tajik delegation, headed by Rustami Emomali, Chairman of the National Assembly, arrived in Uzbekistan for an official visit. The delegation visited the "New Uzbekistan" park, laid flowers at the Independence Monument, and reviewed the development concept for the city of New Tashkent. They also visited the "New Uzbekistan" University.

item.title: Rosatom Develops Lithium Extraction Technology for Uzbekistan
item.description: Russia's Rosatom has developed a waste-free technology for extracting lithium from mica ores at the Nurlikon deposit in Uzbekistan. The new method produces high-purity lithium carbonate and utilizes industrial waste, such as phosphogypsum from the Almalyk Chemical Plant, for intermediate processes. This innovation aims to process 750,000 tons of ore annually.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Economy Ministry Withdraws Proposed Alcohol Excise Tax Increase
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Economy and Commerce has withdrawn a draft resolution to increase excise tax rates on alcoholic beverages. The document, initially proposed to raise taxes on still wines fourfold and sparkling wines twofold, is being sent back for revision. The ministry did not specify the reasons for the revision.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan Strengthen Regional Security Cooperation
item.description: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan held their eighth round of Security Council consultations in Shymkent, focusing on enhancing cooperation against modern threats. Discussions included countering terrorism, extremism, radicalization, organized crime, drug trafficking, illegal migration, and cybercrime. They also addressed challenges from digital technologies and AI, water and environmental security, and transboundary water resource management.

item.title: Uzbekistan Adopts Green Economy Strategy Amid Global Climate Concerns
item.description: Uzbekistan is revising its economic growth model in response to global warming and resource depletion. The country is adopting a green economy strategy focused on low-carbon development, resource efficiency, and social inclusivity, aligning with international sustainable development goals and the Paris Agreement.

item.title: Turkmenistan Arrests Merchants Suspected of Smuggling Tobacco and Drugs
item.description: Authorities in Turkmenistan's Balkan region have detained at least two merchants suspected of attempting to smuggle large quantities of tobacco and illicit drugs across the border. This follows reports of other merchants being detained in the Ahal region for allegedly smuggling narcotics into the country.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Metan Stations and Greenhouses Top List for Illegal Gas Consumption
item.description: Metan filling stations and greenhouses are the largest consumers of illegally obtained gas in Uzbekistan, according to "O'zenergoinspeksiya." Officials identified 900 billion soums worth of illegal gas and electricity use in 10 months. The private sector's share in natural gas misappropriation is significant.

item.title: Kazakhstan Discusses Second Nuclear Plant Deal with China
item.description: Kazakhstan is in talks with China National Nuclear Corporation regarding the construction of a second nuclear power plant, "Moynkum." The first plant, "Balkhash," will be built with a Russian consortium. Both facilities are targeted for completion by 2035.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon Approves Significant Personnel Reshuffle
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon has signed decrees and orders for significant personnel changes affecting various government positions. These changes include leadership roles in cities, districts, and state institutions across the country. The reshuffle impacts judicial, administrative, and regional leadership positions, with some officials released due to reaching retirement age or moving to new roles.

item.title: US Official Discusses Cooperation with Turkmenistan in Ashgabat
item.description: US Assistant Secretary of State for South and Central Asian Affairs, S. Pol Kapur, met with Chairman of the People's Maslakhat Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow in Ashgabat. Kapur also co-chaired annual Turkmen-US political consultations with Foreign Minister Rashid Meredow. Discussions focused on deepening cooperation in trade, investment, energy, education, and cultural exchange.
